passages.speaker: Alex
passages.text: I’d like us to step back and think about what a good meeting actually feels like. We should be listening to each other, not racing to write everything down.

passages.speaker: Maya
passages.text: Exactly. The goal is to be a little more present. Let the tools remember the details, so we can focus on the conversation. And our conversations should stay on our own devices.

passages.speaker: Alex
passages.text: Let’s keep the first version simple. Record a conversation, get a transcript, then turn it into a summary with decisions and next steps. Every note should point back to what was actually said.

passages.speaker: Jordan
passages.text: I can put together a draft of the onboarding flow by Friday. We should make it clear where recordings are stored and let people try recording before they download a model.

passages.speaker: Maya
passages.text: I’ll review the first-use experience and the microphone permission flow. If someone says no to microphone access, we need to explain how to turn it on again.

passages.speaker: Alex
passages.text: That sounds good. We’ve agreed to keep processing local, make each note traceable, and prioritize a calm first-use experience. Let’s review the draft together next week.

summary.text: The team explored a calmer meeting experience: stay present in the conversation while Echo captures the details, entirely on your own device.
The first release focuses on a simple journey from recording to a verifiable transcript, summary, and next steps.

decisions.text: Keep meeting processing local and make every generated note traceable to the original conversation.
Allow recording before model setup is complete.

actions.text: Review the first-use experience and microphone permissions.
